input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 conditions our ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing and matching competing offers for Vendor, which operates as a right of first refusal and de facto sole-supplier restriction on Customer. Section 2.1 compounds this with a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights," locking our spend to Vendor for the full three-year term with no performance-based exit — below the walk-away line. Both conflict with Section 12.3, which states Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, or minimum-volume commitment (that clause is favourable and is retained). The redline deletes 7.2 and converts 2.1 to a non-exclusive arrangement in which any minimum is Order Form-specific and reducible on Vendor's service-level or delivery failure, reaching the preferred position while offering the fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove de facto exclusivity: delete match-or-disclose gate on engaging other providers and strip the take-or-pay lock-in
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement to disclose and match third-party offers before engaging another provider and removed the take-or-pay lock-in, since our playbook allows no exclusivity or sole-source obligation on Customer and Section 12.3 already confirms none was given. If you need a volume commitment, we can accept one stated in an Order Form that is non-exclusive and reducible if you miss service levels or delivery dates.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Vendor is a non-exclusive provider of the Services. Any minimum purchase commitment applies only to the extent expressly stated in a signed Order Form, creates no exclusivity or sole-source obligation, and does not limit Customer's right to procure services from any third party. Customer may reduce or terminate a commitment to the extent Vendor fails to meet an applicable service level or delivery date or Customer terminates for Vendor's breach.
